posts.hook: one developer's github account was the way into 1password's backend
posts.caption: 1password says an attacker took customer names and emails but no vault data, an anthropic researcher posted a riemann proof cut from 17 million lines to 76,000, and reports say the justice department never formally investigated jensen huang before his return to nvidia. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: 1password says an attacker stole customer names and emails, ==not passwords or vaults==
slides.desc: a list of confirmed password-manager customers is ideal phishing material, so distrust the emails

slides.title: an anthropic researcher cut the machine-checked riemann proof to ==76,000 lines==
slides.desc: it was 17 million. the readme is plain: machine checks only, no mathematician has read it through

terms.gloss: verified step by step by proof-checking software, here lean

slides.title: openai's math release is nine manuscripts, not one, including a claimed linear programming result
slides.desc: openai calls the collection raw research data and says unformalized results could have issues

terms.gloss: finding the best outcome under a set of straight-line constraints

slides.title: reuters sources: the justice department ran no formal investigation of huang before his return
slides.desc: washington post sources: pentagon officials discussed an emergency-powers law as leverage on the board

slides.title: 42 state attorneys general oppose character.ai's plan to auction data from 21 million us accounts
slides.desc: over 2.1 million are registered to minors. private chats become an asset when the company fails

slides.title: coding agents fix a security flaw, then reintroduce it in a new session 26.7% of the time
slides.desc: about as often as agents that never saw it. they can fix security bugs but do not learn from them

slides.title: europe's hera probe finds the asteroid nasa hit in 2022 reshaped and tumbling
slides.desc: the crater is nearly as wide as the 151-meter rock, with hundreds of boulders drifting around it

posts.hook: openai found a billing mistake in its newest models. the fix means subscribers get less
posts.caption: openai says a launch billing error had been discounting gpt-6.2 usage, so astra users now hit limits 40% faster, nvidia told partners to halt ai server shipments to four south-east asian countries, and a google research preprint claims a proved running time for factoring integers, unchecked outside google. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: openai corrects a gpt-6.2 billing mistake: astra users now hit their limits ==40% faster==
slides.desc: sol users 25% faster. subscribers calibrated their work to an allowance that was never real

slides.title: ft sources: nvidia tells partners to halt ai server shipments to four south-east asian countries
slides.desc: malaysia, singapore, thailand and indonesia, as the us tightens export controls aimed at china

slides.title: a google research preprint claims a proved running time for factoring integers
slides.desc: written by an ai agent, unchecked outside google. a claim about proof, ==not a new attack on rsa==

terms.gloss: splitting a number into its primes, which much encryption relies on
a widely used encryption scheme that depends on factoring being slow

slides.title: microsoft: state hackers in china and north korea have adopted the ai hacking tool artex
slides.desc: it probes networks for ways in without a human steering each step. assume probing at machine speed

slides.title: bloomberg sources: sap is preparing to cut at least 10,000 jobs, about 9% of its staff
slides.desc: the plan is framed as reshaping its software business for ai: a reason to shrink, not only to add

terms.gloss: a german maker of the business software large companies run on

slides.title: google will make many android developers publish a phone number and address
slides.desc: an eu consumer rule applied worldwide. for a solo developer, the business address is home

slides.title: some memory chip prices have risen tenfold in a year, the wall street journal reports
slides.desc: companies are setting up dedicated buying teams, and electronics prices are rising with them
